source.title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory

accepted.question_text: Construct rational two-dimensional conformal field theories that satisfy the axioms proposed by Kontsevich, Graeme Segal, and Moore-Seiberg, or at least prove that such rational conformal field theories exist. In particular, construct the Wess-Zumino-Witten models and the minimal models, or prove their existence as conformal field theories satisfying those axioms.
accepted.context_brief: Rational conformal field theories and foundational axioms

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Construct rational conformal field theories satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich, G. Segal [Se] and Moore-Seiberg [MS1] [MS2], or at least prove the existence of such rational conformal field theories. In particular, construct the Wess-Zumino-Witten models and minimal models or at least prove their existence.

accepted.question_text: Prove convergence of the series built from intertwining operators that are intended to define higher-genus correlation functions, so that these series can be used to construct higher-genus correlation functions in rational conformal field theory.
accepted.context_brief: Higher-genus correlation functions

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Prove the convergence of these series obtained using intertwining operators to construct higher-genus correlation functions.

accepted.question_text: Suppose the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has an inner product that is invariant under the conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators. Is the locally convex topological completion obtained by adjoining elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces isomorphic, as a locally convex topological vector space with grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form, to the Hilbert space completion of that graded state space?
accepted.context_brief: Comparing two completions of the state space

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.3. If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has a compatible inner product, then the locally convex topological completion obtained by adding elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces and the Hilbert space completion are isomorphic as locally convex topological vector spaces with grading structures and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian forms.

accepted.question_text: For a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length completely reducible if and only if, for every positive integer n, the nth cohomology of the algebra with coefficients in any bimodule vanishes? In particular, for a grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, is complete reducibility of every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length equivalent to vanishing of the nth cohomology for every positive integer n and every bimodule whose left and right actions may differ?
accepted.context_brief: Cohomology criterion for complete reducibility

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. Every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length for a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if for n ∈ Z+, the n-th cohomology of the meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any bimodule is 0. In particular, every grading-restricted generalized module of finite length for a grading-restricted vertex algebra is completely reducible if and only if for n ∈ Z+, the n-th cohomology of the grading-restricted vertex algebra viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any bimodule (whose left and right actions can be different) is 0.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra associated to a Wess-Zumino-Witten model, a minimal model, a lattice vertex operator algebra, or the moonshine module vertex operator algebra. For every positive integer n and every V-bimodule, does the nth cohomology of V, viewed as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra, vanish?
accepted.context_brief: Vanishing cohomology for standard vertex operator algebras

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let V be a vertex operator algebra associated to a Wess-Zumino-Witten model, a minimal model, a lattice vertex operator algebra or the moonshine module vertex operator algebra. Then for n ∈ Z+, the n-th cohomology of V as a meromorphic open-string vertex algebra with coefficients in any V -bimodule is 0.

accepted.question_text: Find a criterion stated purely in terms of a grading-restricted vertex algebra itself that guarantees complete reducibility of its modules.
accepted.context_brief: Intrinsic criterion for complete reducibility

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3. Find a criterion on a grading-restricted vertex algebra itself for the complete reducibility of modules.

accepted.question_text: Study the moduli space of two-dimensional conformal field theories by giving it topological and geometric structures, and prove that rational conformal field theories appear as isolated points in that moduli space.
accepted.context_brief: Moduli space of conformal field theories

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Study the moduli space of conformal field theories. Give topological and geometric structures on the moduli space. Prove that rational conformal field theories are isolated points in the moduli space.

accepted.question_text: Determine conditions under which formal deformations of grading-restricted vertex algebras converge to analytic deformations, and extend the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras to a deformation theory for genus-zero full conformal field theories.
accepted.context_brief: Deformation theory and analytic convergence

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Find the conditions for the formal deformations of grading-restricted vertex algebras to converge to analytic deformations. Generalize the deformation theory of grading-restricted vertex algebras to a deformation theory of genus-zero full conformal field theories.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a simple vertex operator algebra such that V(0)=C1, V(n)=0 for n<0, the contragredient V′ is equivalent to V as a V-module, and V is C2-cofinite. Is the braided tensor category obtained in Huang's logarithmic tensor category theory for grading-restricted generalized V-modules rigid?
accepted.context_brief: Rigidity in logarithmic conformal field theory

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. Assume that V is a simple vertex operator algebra satisfying the following conditions: (1) V(0) = C1, V(n) = 0 for n < 0 and the contragredient V', as a V -module, is equivalent to V. (2) V is C2-cofinite, that is, dim V /C2(V ) < ∞ ... Then the braided tensor category given in [H8] based on the work [HLZ1]-[HLZ9] is rigid.

accepted.question_text: Give an appropriate definition of modular tensor category in the nonsemisimple setting, prove that the braided tensor category arising in Conjecture 5.1 has such a structure, and determine whether such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category still yields a 3-dimensional topological quantum field theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds.
accepted.context_brief: Nonsemisimple modular tensor categories

evidence.quote: Problem 5.2. Give a definition of modular tensor category in the nonsemisimple case and prove that the braided tensor category in Conjecture 5.1 has such a modular tensor category structure. From such a nonsemisimple modular tensor category, can we still construct a 3-dimensional topological quantum field theory and invariants of knots and 3-manifolds?

accepted.question_text: For a vertex operator algebra satisfying the assumptions of Conjecture 5.1, can one construct genus-zero and genus-one full correlation functions from the corresponding genus-zero and genus-one chiral correlation functions? If so, can these be used to construct a conformal field theory satisfying the Kontsevich-Segal axioms except for the axioms involving unitarity?
accepted.context_brief: Full correlation functions in logarithmic CFT

evidence.quote: Problem 5.3. For a vertex operator algebra satisfying the conditions in Conjecture 5.1, is it possible to construct genus-zero and genus-one full correlation functions from the genus-zero and genus-one chiral correlation functions? From these genus-zero and genus-one correlation functions, is it possible to construct a conformal field theory satisfying the axioms of Kontsevich-Segal, except for the axioms involving unitarity?

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the two conditions in Conjecture 5.1, and assume in addition that every grading-restricted generalized V-module is completely reducible. If G is a finite group of automorphisms of V, do twisted intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance?
accepted.context_brief: Twisted intertwining operators for finite orbifolds

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.1. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the two conditions in Conjecture 5.1. Assume that in addition every grading-restricted generalized V -module is completely reducible. Let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V . Then the twisted intertwining operators among the g-twisted V -modules for all g ∈ G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the three conditions in Conjecture 6.1, and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. Is the collection of g-twisted V-modules for all g in G a G-crossed tensor category in the sense of Turaev?
accepted.context_brief: G-crossed category of twisted modules

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.2. Let V be a vertex operator satisfying the three conditions in Conjecture 6.1 and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V . The the category of g-twisted V -modules for all g ∈ G is a G-crossed (tensor) category in the sense of Turaev [T2].

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the two conditions in Conjecture 5.1, and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V. Do twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance?
accepted.context_brief: Logarithmic twisted intertwining operators

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.3. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the two conditions in Conjecture 5.1 and let G be a finite group of automorphisms of V . Then the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V -modules for all g ∈ G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra and G a group of automorphisms of V. When G is infinite, under what conditions do twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V-modules for all g in G satisfy associativity, commutativity, and modular invariance, and under what conditions does the collection of all such g-twisted V-modules form a G-crossed tensor category?
accepted.context_brief: Infinite-group orbifold conditions

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4. Let V be a vertex operator algebra and let G be a group of automorphisms of V . If G is an infinite group, under what conditions do the twisted logarithmic intertwining operators among the g-twisted V -modules for all g ∈ G satisfy the associativity, commutativity and modular invariance properties? Under what conditions is the category of g-twisted V -modules for all g ∈ G a G-crossed (tensor) category?

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra of central charge 24 with no nonzero elements of weight 1, such that every irreducible V-module is equivalent to V itself and every V-module is completely reducible. Must V be isomorphic to the moonshine module vertex operator algebra?
accepted.context_brief: Uniqueness of the moonshine module VOA

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.1. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the following three conditions: (1) The central charge of V is 24. (2) V has no nonzero elements of weight 1. (3) Any irreducible V module is equivalent to V as a V -module and every V -module is completely reducible. Then V must be isomorphic to the moonshine module vertex operator algebra.

accepted.question_text: Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the first and third conditions of Conjecture 7.1, namely central charge 24 and complete reducibility with V as the only irreducible V-module. Is V uniquely determined by the Lie algebra structure on its homogeneous subspace of weight 1?
accepted.context_brief: Classification at central charge 24

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.2. Let V be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the first and the third conditions in Conjecture 7.1. Then V is determined uniquely by the Lie algebra structure on its homogeneous subspace of weight 1.

accepted.question_text: Construct a functor from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras such that the Fermat quintic threefold is sent to the N = 2 vertex operator superalgebra of the Gepner model, and such that deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds correspond to deformations of N = 2 superconformal field theories.
accepted.context_brief: Calabi-Yau manifolds to N=2 VO superalgebras

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1. Construct a functor from the category of Calabi-Yau manifolds to the category of N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras such that the Fermat quintic threefold corresponds to the N = 2 vertex operator superalgebra for the Gepner model and such that deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds correspond to deformations of N = 2 superconformal field theories.

accepted.question_text: Assuming N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras associated to Calabi-Yau manifolds can be constructed, develop their representation theory and use it to build the corresponding N = 2 superconformal field theories, including proofs of the operator product expansion for intertwining operators, modular invariance, construction of modular tensor categories in an appropriate sense, and construction of full N = 2 superconformal field theories.
accepted.context_brief: Representation theory for Calabi-Yau superconformal models

evidence.quote: Problem 8.2. If N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manifolds can be constructed, study the representation theory of these N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras. Use this representation theory to construct the corresponding N = 2 superconformal field theories, including the proof of the operator product expansion of intertwining operators, the proof of modular invariance, the construction of modular tensor categories (in a suitable sense), and the construction of full N = 2 superconformal field theories.

accepted.question_text: Assuming one can construct N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras associated to Calabi-Yau manifolds, obtain the basic representation-theoretic results for them, and construct the corresponding full N = 2 superconformal field theories, formulate and prove physicists' conjectures on Calabi-Yau manifolds, such as quantum cohomology and mirror symmetry, by converting the physical intuition into mathematical methods based on those constructions.
accepted.context_brief: Mathematical proofs of Calabi-Yau physics conjectures

evidence.quote: Problem 8.3. Suppose that N = 2 vertex operator superalgebras corresponding to Calabi-Yau manidfolds can be constructed, that the basic results in the representation theory of these algebras can be obtained and that the full N = 2 superconformal field theories can be constructed. Formulate and prove the conjectures (for example, quantum cohomology and mirror symmetry) by physicists on Calabi-Yau manifolds by turning physicists’ intuition into mathematical methods using these results and constructions.

accepted.question_text: Find a direct connection between the representation-theoretic approach via vertex operator algebras and the operator-algebraic approach via conformal nets, and prove that at least in the case of rational conformal field theories the two approaches are equivalent.
accepted.context_brief: Vertex operator algebras versus conformal nets

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1. Find a direct connection between the method of the representation theory of vertex operator algebras and the method of conformal nets. Prove that at least for rational conformal field theories, they are equivalent.
